conventions: Where the ASV writes one volitive frame over a run of coordinated jussives or prohibitives (v.1 *keep not thou … Hold not thy peace … be not still*; v.17 *Let them be put to shame and dismayed … let them be confounded and perish*), the frame joins the first verb of the coordination under rule 17 and each later verb takes only its own lexical word and the negative or connective written for it; the frame is not repeated onto later verbs and no part of it is `added`.
report: Read all 14 candidate lemmas end to end. Every difference is licensed by the ASV's own rendering: the waws take whichever connective is written for them (and/That/Yea/And), the כְּ of vv.9 and 11 differ because the ASV writes one *like* per coordinated pair in v.11 (the repeated כְּ is unrepresented under rule 22) but an *as* for each member in v.9, and the suffix treatments (them/their/thy/thine/whose/unrepresented) each answer to what the ASV wrote in that verse.

No cross-verse split found. The two constructions that recur most — the supplied relative over an asyndetic finite clause with a written antecedent (vv.10 *Who* ×2, v.14 *that* ×2, all `added` under rules 46/55) and the jussive/prohibitive frame shared across coordinated verbs (vv.1, 17, frame on the first verb, later verbs take only their lexical word) — are handled identically in every verse they touch.

The `added` units were checked against the dump: the four are all supplied relatives (vv.10, 14); no verse folds the same supplied relative into a neighbouring morpheme. The only 3-morpheme noncompositional unit (v.8 הָיוּ זְרוֹעַ לִ → *They have helped*) is genuinely indivisible — no English word writes any one morpheme's lexeme — and the margin's literal gloss corroborates the fusion.

Single-verse judgments left standing with their alternatives noted: v.1 *keep* on the possessive לְ (rules 43/49), v.1 *thy* of *Hold thy peace* inside the verb's fixed idiom (rule 30), v.4 *being* as the construction copula on גּוֹי (rule 20), v.9 the four *unto/to* on the one dative לְ as a distributed repetition (rule 25, modelled on *search for her as for hid treasures*), v.17 עֲדֵי־עַד split *for*/*ever* under rule 2. None is a chapter-wide inconsistency.

BSB disagreements (6): all convention differences, none an error — v.2 paragogic nun (rule 32); v.11 object suffix מוֹ resumed by the appositional *their nobles*, whose possessive is the noun's own suffix (rule 22); v.11 the two repeated כְּ the ASV renders once per pair (rule 22); v.12 object marker (rule 16); v.18 suffix of לְבַדֶּךָ, whose *thou* belongs to the explicit אַתָּה (rule 40).
No promotions or amendments: the chapter teaches nothing general the contract does not already state.
